Procedure

1Confirm there is stock

Result
Know what you can actually ship.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Inventory 360 shows what's on hand, and Allocated shows how much of it other orders have already claimed. Stock is often spread across several warehouses. The sales order has to name one that holds enough, or LN won't find stock to pick. This task is where you choose that warehouse.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Type the item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it, showing On Hand · Blocked · On Order · Allocated
1.2Tick the item's own rowThe header links become available
1.3In the Inventory group of the header, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory (whwmd2515m000) opens with the item already filled in
1.4Read Inventory on Hand and Inventory Allocated per warehouseThe totals are under the gridWrite downitemwarehouseon-handallocated

2Create and approve the sales order

Result
The order status is In Process.
Screen
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. Only approved lines can be released to warehousing. If you skip approval, the release may fail later without a clear reason. The Order Acknowledgement that prints shows the sales order number, and the warehousing order uses the same number.

StepActionYou should see
2.1In the header, click New
2.2Enter your customer as Sold-to Business Partner, press TabAddress fills in
2.3Select the Order TypeExampleOrder Type N10 — Standard orders (no ATP)
2.4Set Planned Delivery Date and Planned Receipt DateExamplePlanned Delivery Date 2026-10-23 — left at the order datePlanned Receipt Date 2026-10-23 — left at the planned delivery dateBoth start at the Order Date
2.5Check Sales Office and Site on the Order tab, and Currency on the Invoicing tab
2.6Set Warehouse to the warehouse recorded at step 1.4
2.7Click SaveStatus = FreeWrite downsales order number
2.8In the lines, click New
2.9Search for and select the Item you checked at step 1.4
2.10Enter the Ordered QuantityExampleOrdered Quantity 5Write downordered quantity
2.11Click Save
2.12In the header, Actions➔ApproveStatus = In Process. The Order Acknowledgement prints. For an item that needs documents, a Conformance Reporting sheet prints too
Create and approve the sales order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Status stuck on FreeThe order isn't approved yet. Choose Actions➔Approve
The order can't be approved yetIf Use Confirmation is selected on the order's terms and conditions or on the sold-to business partner, the customer has to confirm the goods first.
On-hand looks high enough, but the order won't fillCheck Allocated: other orders may already have claimed most of the on-hand. See step 1.4

3Release to warehousing

Result
A warehousing order exists.
Screen
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. Releasing passes the approved lines from Sales to Warehousing. LN creates a warehousing order with the sales order's number, and from then on the warehousing procedure decides what happens next, not the sales order. You release from the Actions menu; the Lines ready for panel only counts lines.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Select your order in the Sales Orders grid
3.2Actions➔Release➔Release to Warehousing…The release session opens
3.3Set Upto Release Date on or after the order line's Release Date — it defaults to the planned delivery date minus the outbound lead time
3.4Leave the Options tickedPrint Errors · Print Released Lines · Print to predefined Device
3.5Click RELEASEThe Log Report prints
3.6Open the Order Lines tab
3.7Find your order and tick it
3.8References➔StatusSales Order Line Status (tdsls4534s000) opens on Activities 1. Release Sales Orders to Warehousing = Executed
Release to warehousing: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Clicking RELEASE TO WAREHOUSING in Lines ready for does nothingThat panel only counts lines. Use Actions➔Release instead
Your order isn't in the releaseUpto Release Date is earlier than the order line's Release Date, which is the planned delivery date minus the outbound lead time. Set a later date
No warehousing orderThe release didn't run. Check Activities 1 at step 3.8. If it reads Free, run it from Actions➔Release
Activity shows Automatic: NoThat activity doesn't run on its own in this configuration. Run it from Actions➔Release➔Release to Warehousing…

4Generate outbound advice

Result
LN knows what to pick, and the picking list prints.
Screen
Warehousing➔Manager Dashboard (whinh2300m000)

Why LN works this way. Generating advice is LN choosing which stock, from which locations, fills each outbound line. In this environment the next activity, releasing the advice, runs on its own, so one action fills both Advised and Released and prints the picking list. That's set by the warehousing order type's outbound procedure.

StepActionYou should see
4.1In the order grid at the bottom, filter Order on your sales order numberSales rows read Origin Sales, Type 20- SO/SC Out, Transaction Type Issue
4.2Tick the row, then click Drill InWarehousing Order (whinh2100m100) opens
4.3Open the Outbound Lines tabLine Status = Open
4.4Tick the outbound line
4.5On the Outbound Lines toolbar, Actions➔Advice➔Generate Advice, then click CONTINUE in the Select Device dialogThe Picking List by Location prints to its own tab. Advised and Released both fill — release is automatic hereWrite downRunMission
4.6Open the Shipment Lines tab and check for an early shipmentIf projected shipments are switched on, a Projected or Open line may already show a value in Shipment. If the tab is empty, go on to Pick the goods. That's normal
Generate outbound advice: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Nothing under Outbound OpenThere's no warehousing order. Go back to Release to warehousing
Your order isn't in the order gridThe Order filter may be wrong, or the release may not have run. See step 3.8
You can't find Outbound Order LinesThere's no menu entry by that name. Filter the Manager Dashboard's order grid and drill in
Advice greyed out on the Actions menuYou're on the session toolbar. The advice actions are on the Outbound Lines toolbar. See step 4.5
Generate Advice greyed outAdvice may already exist. Check Advised Quantity. To start over, use Undo Advice
Release Advice greyed outThere may be no advice yet. Run Generate Advice first
Advice already generated before you ran itSome configurations generate advice on release. Check Advised Quantity first
The outbound line's status reads PlannedA planned line can't be advised. Choose Activate on the warehousing order, and the line becomes Open.
The order won't adviseCheck that the header Warehouse holds the stock, against step 1.4

5Pick the goods

Result
The pick is confirmed in LN, and the stock is in staging.
Screen
Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List (whinh4525m100)

Why LN works this way. The picking list records stock moving to staging, and confirming it fills Picked. You need this task because, in this environment, the Picking List activity is manual and the warehouse is location-controlled. Whether you need this task depends on those two settings; without them, LN ticks Picked on release. Once a line is staged, LN creates the shipment line.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Check Run in the header. If it isn't the Run from step 4.5, click Find, fill in Run and click OKThe Run you wrote down. next / previous step through every run in code order
5.2Confirm Warehouse and MissionMission is the Picking Mission from step 4.5
5.3Read the grid linesOne line per location the stock comes from: Picked · Sequence · Item · Serial Number · From Location. Picked shows a grey dot
5.4Pick the goods on each line from its From Location to its To Location, then tick the lines
5.5Actions➔Pick RunLN records the pick: stock moves from From Location to To Location. Picked fills on Outbound Lines, and the line status becomes Staged
5.6Return to the Warehousing Order, drilling in as at step 4.2, and open Shipment LinesA shipment line now exists. The shipment number is the first part of Shipment Line, before the line's own number:Write downshipment number
Pick the goods: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No Picking node under WarehousingThere isn't one. Picking is under Outbound/Inspections
Goods still need picking after Release AdviceThat's expected. Released and Picked are separate columns. Do this task
Run empty on the Picking ListAdvice may not have been generated, so nothing was released. Go back to step 4.5

6Ship

Result
The shipment is confirmed, and the stock leaves inventory.
Screen
Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments (whinh4130m000)

Why LN works this way. Freezing locks the shipment's contents, and confirming takes the stock out of inventory. The status only changes through those two actions; you can't set it by hand. Freezing is mandatory here, because this warehousing order type requires it. A confirmed shipment can't be changed: to correct it, you need a return shipment.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Find the shipment number from step 5.6, then click Drill InStatus = Open. Freeze Mandatory ticked; Allow Changes to Shipment ticked
6.2Read the Shipped Quantity. To ship less than was picked, change it on Shipment Lines (whinh4131m000), not hereWrite downshipped quantity
6.3Actions➔Freeze (Shift+F)Status = Frozen. Confirm becomes available. A Bill of Lading and the packing slip print, each to its own tab
6.4Open the Packing Slips tab. Check the customer it ships to, the shipment number, the order and line, the item and the shipped quantity against the orderThe details match the order and the quantity you're shipping
6.5Actions➔Confirm (Shift+C)Status = Confirmed. The stock leaves inventory
Ship: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The shipment won't confirmThe line may not be picked. Check the Picked column on Outbound Lines, then do Pick the goods
The shipment won't confirm, and a validation message showsIf the order type validates shipments, fix any message marked Blocking first. If you reopen a frozen shipment, it's validated again.
The shipment won't confirm, and it has handling unitsIf Handling Unit Based Confirmation is set on a linked line, confirm the handling units first. Whether the line then confirms on its own is an order-type setting, Confirm Shipment Lines when confirming Handling Units. If that's cleared, the line stays Frozen until you confirm it

7Verify it worked

Result
On-hand went down by the quantity shipped.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Check the same item and warehouse you checked in Confirm there is stock. This confirms that inventory changed as expected.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Filter the item, tick its row and open Warehouse Inventory, as at steps 1.1–1.3, and read Inventory on Hand for the warehouse you recorded thereWrite downon-hand afterdifference

On-hand before − on-hand after should equal the shipped quantity, in the same unit, as long as nothing else moved the item in that warehouse. On-hand before is the figure from step 1.4. If they differ, check that the shipment reads Confirmed. Then open Item Transactions from Inventory 360 to see what else moved the item. Ship from stock is done when the shipment is Confirmed and the drop in on-hand matches the quantity shipped, after allowing for anything else that moved the item. Invoicing comes next, and this guide doesn't cover it.

Variations

CaseWhat changes
Standalone advice sessionsWarehousing➔Outbound/Inspections holds Generate Outbound Advice and Release Outbound Advice as their own sessions. Use them for a batch of orders rather than one
Direct ReleaseActions➔Advice➔Direct Release is on the same menu as Generate Advice.
UndoingUndo Advice · Undo Release · Undo Advice/Release (Shift+Z)
Pick Mission / Pick Advice
Task 5		Use these to pick one mission or one advice line instead of the whole run. See step 5.5
Shipping less than ordered
Task 6		Reduce Shipped Quantity on Shipment Lines (whinh4131m000); see step 6.2. Once the shipment is confirmed, LN creates a backorder. It becomes a new line only once it's confirmed in Sales.

Known gaps

The library has no source for these yet, so this Document says nothing about them rather than guess.

  • Task 2, if something goes wrong: The order can't be approved yet
  • Task 4, if something goes wrong: The outbound line's status reads Planned
  • Task 6, if something goes wrong: The shipment won't confirm, and a validation message shows
  • Variation: Direct Release
  • Variation: Shipping less than ordered
